16400.description:
Let's meet! Within your residential college, you are also a member of a smaller "zee group" (short for your advisee group), with 15-18 other new students and your RCA (residential college adviser), RGS (resident graduate student), and PAA.

Use this discussion space to introduce yourself to your zee group.

Let us know your name and current location, and share an image that captures something about you.
Upload the image so that your zee group can see it. Use the "Reply" function below to create your post. Do reply and comment on other posts, too! 

Your image could be something meaningful to you, such as your pet or your favorite movie or book. Or, it could be an image that just speaks to you. What does the image mean to you? Feel free to keep your introduction brief, like in our example and your PAA's introduction below!

Example:

Hello, my name is Junhow. I am writing from Philadelphia, PA. I eat ramen noodles all the time and Shin is my favorite brand.

16400.description:
Knowing what you are passionate about can help guide you through your academic choices. Consider these short questions and begin to look for patterns that may shape your Princeton path:

          • What kind of academic work do you gravitate toward first?
          • What sections are you drawn to in a bookstore?
          • Who are the people you admire most? Why?
          • If you could change one thing about your community, what would it be?

Open the Google Docs in the window below and jot down your answers to these questions and any insights about your academic plans at Princeton. Your PAA will offer comments. Have a question now? Reach out to your PAA!

To submit your assignment:

  1. Link your Princeton Google Drive account with Canvas by clicking the "Link" button and following the prompts in the pop-up window. If you are logged in to your personal Google account, you will need to switch accounts first. You will only need to do this once.
  2. Start by clicking the "Open to attach and submit" button.
  3. From the Google Assignments page, click the link to the Google Doc file (e.g., "Name - Action Item 2: Reflecting on Your Path to Princeton").
  4. Write your reflection. Google Docs will automatically save your work, so you can close the window when you're done. 
  5. After completing your reflection, return to the Google Assignments page and click "Submit"!
16400.name: Action Item 2: Reflecting on Your Path to Princeton

19971.description:
Prompt: Salgarolo details how large forces such as colonialism, racial capitalism, and slavery in St. Malo, a small village in Louisiana built by Filipino sailors in the mid-nineteenth century,  reshaped social, cultural and the physical landscapes.

Provide one instance of this reshaping that stood out to you from the lecture and relate it to some of the concepts/keywords we have discussed in our class so far. Be specific!

[500 words / 15 points extra credit to be added to participation grade]

Make sure you email me a photo of you at the event to get full credit!
19971.name: Extra Credit: "Manila Bayou" - Michael Salgarolo Lecture

19971.description:
Prompt: How does Tam play with the concept of labor and the practice of performance and how does that help us think through concepts like Shah's "stranger intimacy" and the way in which social ideas of race, gender, labor, and land are all co-constitutive (all shape and determine one another)? How does Tam's work help us to think through similar dynamics in the present? 

[500 words / 15 extra credit points in the participation category]
19971.name: Extra Credit: "Silent Spikes" by Kenneth Tam

19971.description:
A report back on another site that is facing similar issues of inequitable or harmful development and/or gentrification either on or around campus or elsewhere in New Jersey. The purpose is for you to connect some of the concepts we’ve discussed to your daily environment. (Most ideally, examples you have not brought up already in our group discussions). Your presentation should be able to explain the background and significance of your chosen site to all of us who may be unaware of the context. You are also encouraged to discuss what the opposing views are (eg. those who are in favor of the development). Please bring visuals.

You must also submit here a 750 word write up afterwards that presents your own viewpoint of the development, whether that be for, against, or mixed. This write up should not just be stating opinions but should be backing up your viewpoint through citing theoretical or cultural texts we’ve discussed.
19971.name: Final Presentations Upload (Non-Field Trip Students Only)

19971.description:
Option 1: You may revise your midterm essay by expanding it and adding an additional cultural text for a more comparative analysis of the concept and texts. For example, if you chose Lowe's Intimacies of Four Continents and Pete Pin's "Migrations of Memory" in your midterm, you could then bring in a second cultural text such as Tseng Kwon Chi's photography to discuss the aesthetic, formal and rhetorical strategies of how both artists address the concept of intimacy. The midterm page limit was about 5 pages double spaced, handwritten. The revision should be about 10-12 pages typed, double spaced (approximately 6000 words).

Option 2: You may choose to write an entirely new essay from this prompt: What concept or argument from our course changed your prior thinking about the relationship between power, race and space/placemaking? Or, if you didn't experience any major revelations, what existing belief about power, race, and space/placemaking did you have confirmed and why/how? You must discuss at length one of the theoretical texts we have read and one cultural text from the course or from outside (that you provide a link or access to so that I may view it). This essay should be thesis and argument driven. 

Crucially, for a full grade, you must also reference a discussion we had in class on the same text/topic. This may include: something that a colleague said in one of our discussions that sparked something in your thinking (or that you disagreed with); an example or visual that the instructor brought up; or something that felt unsatisfactory or unexplained in the texts and our discussion of it. Most ideally, you would include more than one of the above as you reference our class discussions. The essay should be 10-12 pages, double spaced.

Based on the Princeton exam schedule, the due date is Thursday, December 18th at 3:30pm
19971.name: Final Essay
